text: {"question":"How does the 0.6‑dex revision of host galaxy masses for the 114 supernovae affect the computation of the distance‑modulus residuals that enter the χ² statistic for the Pantheon+ sample?","reference_answer":"The 0.6‑dex mass correction moves those 114 supernovae from the low‑mass bias‑correction branch to the high‑mass branch, thereby changing their standardized apparent magnitudes (mB) used in the distance modulus µi = mB,i – M. This altered µi modifies the residuals ∆µi (µi – µmodel(zi) for non‑Cepheid hosts) that are summed in the χ² expression, potentially reducing the overall χ² for the Pantheon+ dataset."}
